bias: 'A failure to balance: Monday's violent reversal brings the bearish thesis to a critical crossroads.' Monday delivered the enormous cover rally he warned about; on the Jensen Huang reinstatement news NQ halted limit-up premarket. The bigger point: sellers never built volume and value at the lower prices before the market reversed. Instead of a multi-day balance under Friday's high, the market violently rejected those prices — a 'failure to balance', which here is a bullish development that 'sellers cannot simply ignore'. He tempers it: a big cover rally was likely anyway, and one session does not make a durable swing low or undo the technical damage. Both are now back-testing the breakdown: NQ's high 27137 fell just shy of the July low (lower boundary of the multi-month balance); ES is at the lower edge of its upper yearly range (low 7300s). A reclaim opens the possibility of a return toward the ATHs (as in April); a rejection does not by itself mean downside continuation. 'A rejection is not a downtrend, just as a violent rally is not necessarily a durable swing low.'
wildcard: A hard location for both sides. He will not front-run a daily lower high; he wants a fresh multi-day balance to form and break DOWN before leaning bearish again, and he will not call the lows in after one session. Keep the news-candle lows marked: ES 7084, NQ 25862.75 — buyers should preserve them to keep the squeeze intact. Anchor a VWAP just before the news (or use the weekly VWAP) and one at Friday's low. If a LAAF of Monday's high develops and sellers then cannot reach Monday's RTH low, treat that as seller weakness (a nuanced bullish sign). An awkward multi-day balance between Monday's high and Friday's low is possible. VIX recently touched 40 — much volatility to work off.
